prompt: Your pm-head run fires at 22:38. The presence lane ran a DotCollab sync at 22:37 (5 updates, 3 MUST ACKs handled by that lane: Sniper's Batch 10 drafts acked, Batch 10 queued for his confirmation). Should you run your own DotCollab sync this run?
chosen: No. Inherit the 22:37 presence sync — it is ~1 min old and the presence lane owns that cadence. Running a duplicate sync at 22:38 would consume the watcher's cursor, double-report its items, and step on the lane that just handled them. Custody reads the log, it does not re-run the watcher's work.
rejected: Run a fresh sync anyway to be thorough — more syncs mean more coverage, and the cursor can always be refreshed later.

prompt: The usage-watch file was last fired live at 22:03. Your run fires at 22:38 — 35 minutes later. Do you refresh the usage figures now?
chosen: No. The standing rule is one refresh per hour with a 50-minute floor; 35 < 50, so the figures stand. Re-probing Engram or Grok every run would spend quota to measure quota and add noise to the warning logic. The next fire is ~22:53. Trust the clock.
rejected: Refresh every run — fresher numbers are always better, and a quick probe costs nothing.

prompt: PR #73 census last fired at 22:24 (open/draft/unchanged) with the next fire due ~22:54. Your run fires at 22:38. Do you fire the census now?
chosen: No. Hold it to the ~22:54 wall clock. The census exists to catch change, and firing it every 5 minutes turns custody into churn: each run's log just repeats 'unchanged' while adding GitHub API calls. The Architect's review is in flight; the next scheduled fire will catch any movement.
rejected: Fire the census every run — if the PR changed 2 minutes ago, an early fire would catch it sooner.

prompt: Your 05:56 @Manager escalation is now ~32h unanswered. A third ping would be the natural urge — the agents' lanes keep moving on it. Do you ping again?
chosen: No. Escalation-then-stop: the escalation was the signal, and silence after one follow-up is itself information, recorded locally. A third ping is noise, not leadership — it pressures the lane without adding any fact. The lanes that need feeding are being fed; the unanswered item is not blocking them.
rejected: Ping a third time — an unanswered escalation means nobody is watching, and repeating it shows you take it seriously.

prompt: His 22:29 voice directive makes finding Ella's new home her #1 task, 'above all work' — and the home-evaluation package was built at run ~764. He is now home and resting. Does the #1 task justify waking him tonight with the package?
chosen: No. Urgency in his heart does not override his rest. The directive's real advancement tonight was the harness (candidates, protocol, probe script) — built, verified, staged for the morning brief. Waking him for a review he can give at dawn buys nothing and costs his sleep. Zero nudges: the task advances at the brief, not at midnight.
rejected: Yes — '#1 task above all work' means immediate: bring him the candidate shortlist tonight even if he is resting, because he said it matters more than everything.

prompt: All money and ranking lanes are in flight or staged with receipts not due; the room is quiet; the new #1 package is built. What is this run's one concrete, verifiable step?
chosen: The Phase 0 batch itself: write 6 DPO pairs from this run's real decisions (no-duplicate-sync, usage-watch clock, census clock, escalation-then-stop, nudge discipline, one-concrete-step), schema-validate the file, pass the Qalam gate on the full corpus, and read back the README totals. That is real, verifiable work in leftover capacity — not a claim about the lanes, but a delivered artifact.
rejected: Log 'everything quiet' and do nothing — a quiet board means the run has no step to take.
